2027-02-06.title: Saturday after Aneede Sunday
readings: Rich in good works, generous and ready to share
The rich fool: rich toward God
2027-02-06.alt: Season of Denho. Tomorrow is Kothine Sunday, the first Sunday of the Great Fast, and Catholicos Day.
2027-02-06.verse: So it is with those who store up treasures for themselves but are not rich toward God.
theo: Jesus tells a story about a successful farmer. “The land of a rich man produced abundantly,” and he has a problem every farmer would like to have: no room for the harvest. So he plans: “I will pull down my barns and build larger ones… And I will say to my soul, Soul, you have ample goods laid up for many years; relax, eat, drink, be merry.” He talks only to himself; there is no God in his plan and no neighbour. “But God said to him, ‘You fool! This very night your life is being demanded of you. And the things you have prepared, whose will they be?’” Jesus does not condemn the harvest. He condemns the barn that has no door to the poor: “So it is with those who store up treasures for themselves but are not rich toward God.”

Paul gives Timothy the positive side of the same teaching. The rich are not to be haughty, nor “to set their hopes on the uncertainty of riches, but rather on God who richly provides us with everything for our enjoyment. They are to do good, to be rich in good works, generous, and ready to share,” and so “take hold of the life that really is life.” This is the last Saturday before the Great Fast. Fasting without almsgiving would only fill a different barn. St Basil the Great, preaching on this parable, said that the bread we store belongs to the hungry and the coat in our chest belongs to the one who has none (in substance). Tomorrow, Catholicos Day, our Church asks every parish to share for the needs of the whole Church; it is a good place to begin being rich toward God.
outline: Ask: if your life were demanded of you tonight, whose would your things be?
Point 2 · You fool, this very night
A plan with no God and no neighbour.
live: Set aside a fixed portion of your money for the poor for the whole Fast.
Give generously at tomorrow's Catholicos Day collection.
2027-02-06.prayer: Lord God, you richly provide us with everything. Free us from hoping in uncertain riches and from barns built only for ourselves. Make us rich in good works, generous and ready to share, so that we may take hold of the life that really is life. Bless our Major Archbishop-Catholicos and our whole Church as we begin the Great Fast. Amen.
altar: At the altar we bring bread and wine, gifts God first gave us, and he returns them as the Bread of life for all.

quick: The rich fool planned only for himself and forgot God.
Paul tells the rich to hope in God and be generous.
2027-02-06.action: Set aside money for the poor for the whole Great Fast.
2027-02-06.question: Whom does my barn have room for?

family.explain: A rich man had so much grain that he built bigger barns, but he never thought of God or of hungry people. Jesus says the real treasure is being rich toward God, sharing with others.
family.intention: We pray for families who do not have enough food today.
family.ask: Ask: “What can we share during the Great Fast, as a family?”

illus: A rubber planter near Ranni kept a small box beside the family altar. Every Lent each member of the family put into it whatever they saved by fasting: the price of a meal, a film, a new shirt. On Pesaha they opened it together and decided whom to help. One year it paid a poor neighbour's daughter's school fees. The children remembered that box long after they forgot the food they had given up.

pm.open: Lord, you give us all good things. Make us rich toward you. Amen.
share: Not to set their hopes on the uncertainty of riches (1 Timothy 6:17). Where is my security?
Soul, you have ample goods laid up for many years (Luke 12:19). What am I storing up?
Rich in good works, generous, and ready to share (1 Timothy 6:18). What will I give in the Fast?
pm.resp: Lord, make us rich toward you.
interc: For the poor and hungry in our town.
For our Major Archbishop-Catholicos and the Catholicos Day collection.
For farmers and all who work the land.
For those who trust in money more than in God.
For the grace of a good Great Fast for our parish.
pm.close: Father, all we have comes from your hand. Teach us to share it with joy, so that we may be rich toward you and take hold of true life. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, the rich man in the parable had a good harvest and a simple plan: bigger barns and a comfortable life. He spoke only to his own soul (Luke 12:18–19).
God said to him: You fool! This very night your life is being demanded of you. And the things you have prepared, whose will they be? (Luke 12:20). His barn had no door to God or to the poor.
Paul tells Timothy to command the rich not to hope in uncertain riches but in God, and to be rich in good works, generous, and ready to share (1 Timothy 6:17–18).
Tomorrow the Great Fast begins in our Sunday worship, and it is also Catholicos Day. Let us open our barns: fasting with almsgiving, so that we may be rich toward God. Amen.
kids: Children, a rich man built bigger and bigger barns for himself, but forgot God and the hungry. During the Great Fast, can you save something and share it with someone who needs it?

intro: On the eve of the Great Fast, the Church puts almsgiving beside fasting.

q: Put no confidence in extortion, and set no vain hopes on robbery; if riches increase, do not set your heart on them.

As for those who in the present age are rich, command them not to be haughty, or to set their hopes on the uncertainty of riches, but rather on God who richly provides us with everything for our enjoyment.
points.apply: Thank God today for three things money cannot buy.

q: Do not be afraid when some become rich, when the wealth of their houses increases. For when they die they will carry nothing away; their wealth will not go down after them.
But God said to him, ‘You fool! This very night your life is being demanded of you. And the things you have prepared, whose will they be?’
points.apply: Decide what you will give away this Lent, not only what you will give up.

sub: A good foundation for the future.
The life that really is life.
q: Whoever is kind to the poor lends to the Lord, and will be repaid in full.
They are to do good, to be rich in good works, generous, and ready to share,
points.apply: Give generously at the Catholicos Day collection tomorrow.

concl: A life that stores up only for itself is foolish before God.
Generosity is the true wealth that lasts.
2027-02-06.resolve: Keep a Lenten box for the poor at home from tomorrow until Pesaha.
